candidates: Morning glory optic disc anomaly with chronic retinal detachment
key_facts: Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina was observed
Chronic retinal detachment was found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple, iridescent, needle-like crystals floating freely within the aqueous of the right eye is characteristic of Synchysis scintillans.

rejected.label: Morning glory optic disc anomaly with chronic retinal detachment
rejected.why: While the patient has a morning glory optic disc anomaly and chronic retinal detachment, these findings do not explain the presence of crystals in the aqueous humor.

rejected.label: Coats disease
rejected.why: Coats disease typically presents with retinal telangiectasia and exudation, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cholesterolosis
rejected.why: Cholesterolosis is a rare condition that can cause crystals in the eye, but the description of the crystals as iridescent and needle-like is more consistent with Synchysis scintillans.
